verdicts.title: The four Session charts are computed over three different frame populations; the guiding chart includes frames the app rejected
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced independently on my own profile (v-analytics, display :83) with the same seeded DB. Analytics > Session > Night A - M31 renders exactly the claimed headers: Image quality n=10, Guiding performance median 0.8 / p90 3.9 / range 0.5-4.2 / n=12, Focus drift n=12, Sensor temperature n=16, while the session strip reads EXPOSURES 10/12. I recomputed the populations straight from sqlite rather than from another app readout: session 1 holds 12 lights (10 with is_accepted=1 and guiding_rms_total 0.50..0.95, 2 with is_accepted=0 and hfr 9.9 / rms 4.2 / focuser 15100) plus 4 darks whose only non-null metric is sensor_temp -10.0. So HFR sees 10 rows, guiding and focuser see 12 (the two rejects included), temperature sees 16 (the four darks included). Guiding p90 over the accepted 10 is 0.905 by linear interpolation; over all 12 it is 3.875, which the UI rounds to the 3.9 on screen - a 4.3x overstatement that also breaches the 1.0-arcsec warn line GuidingRmsChart draws. The where: is exact - session_chart.dart:375 is `.where((img) => img.hfr != null && img.isAccepted)`, :400 sensorTemp, :425 guidingRmsTotal, :453 focuserPosition, none of which filters isAccepted or frameType. I also saw the mirror-image symptom on session 5 (2 rejected lights): the HFR card reads 'No HFR (px) recorded for these frames' while guiding/focus/temperature all report n=2 for those same frames.

verdicts.title: Captured Images grades dark/calibration frames as "Good", inflating the session quality summary
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced. The Captured Images chips on Night A - M31 read Good: 12 / Needs Review: 2 / Poor: 2 / Total: 16, and the accessibility tree of the rail lists, in order, 8 light tiles badged GOOD (75 score), 2 NEEDS REVIEW (63 score, hfr 3.6/3.8), 2 POOR/REJECTED (0 score, hfr 9.9), then 4 tiles badged 'GOOD / - / 300s / 75 score' with no HFR and an em-dash filter. Those last four are the darks: sqlite confirms rows 13-16 are frame_type='dark' with hfr, star_count, guiding_rms_total and quality_score all NULL. The mechanism is exactly as cited - frame_quality_assessment_service.dart:112 is verbatim `var advisoryScore = image.qualityScore ?? 75.0;`, and with every metric null nothing decrements it, so a frame with zero quality measurement lands on FrameQualityLevel.good; image_thumbnail_strip.dart:90 is verbatim `final assessments = assessor.assessBatch(widget.images);` over the unfiltered list. Both file:line citations are correct. Only 8 of 16 frames were actually assessed good, so 'Good: 12' is a false count. Severity corrected down to P2: the panel is explicitly labelled advisory ('Quality labels are advisory only. No frames are deleted or auto-rejected'), the darks are distinguishable by their em-dash filter and blank HFR, and no capture, reject or scheduling decision is driven off this number - it misstates a summary rather than costing a night.

verdicts.title: Exported FWHM is fabricated from HFR with the wrong factor (2.35x instead of 2x), overstating FWHM by 18%
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with my own fresh export rather than the reporter's file: Analytics > History > Night A - M31 > fileSpreadsheet icon wrote /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/Night A - M31_2026-08-02T12-05-18.csv, and every row's FWHM/HFR ratio is exactly 2.35 (2.00->4.70, 3.80->8.93, 9.90->23.27). sqlite confirms `select count(*), count(fwhm) from captured_images where session_id=1` = 16|0, i.e. the fwhm column is NULL for every exported row, so the column is fabricated. session_export_service.dart:70 is verbatim `final fwhm = image.hfr != null ? image.hfr! * 2.35 : null;` and :171 repeats it for the JSON export; session_report_service.dart:301 and capture_preview_loader.dart:180 carry the same factor. I checked the physics claim independently instead of taking it on trust: native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/stats.rs:672 documents and implements `calculate_hfr_at_point` as the true encircled-energy 50% half-flux RADIUS ('matches the NINA / SGP / PixInsight HFR convention'), and for a Gaussian the 50%-encircled-energy radius is sqrt(2 ln 2)*sigma = 1.1774*sigma while FWHM = 2.3548*sigma, so FWHM = 2.000*HFR. Multiplying by 2.3548 treats a radius as a sigma and inflates every number by 17.74% - matching the finding's 17.7%. The claim that the measured column is discarded also holds beyond this seed: imaging_service/persistence.dart:196 and imaging_records_repository.dart:420 do write a real `fwhm`, and the exporter never reads it. Two nits for the fixer, neither changing the verdict: the evidence path in the finding (..._2026-08-01T14-40-26.csv) does not exist - the reporter's actual file is ..._2026-08-01T14-39-48.csv; and the cited range 69-70 is really line 70 (69 is the comment).

verdicts.title: Insights invents a guiding baseline of 0.1 arcsec when there is no history, so every user with <=5 sessions is told their guiding degraded 7x
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced verbatim. Analytics > Science > Insights shows 'Guiding degradation - Recent guiding RMS is 7.20x the historical baseline. Check balance, flexure, and backlash.' and 'Focus quality drift - Recent median HFR is elevated versus the longer-term baseline.' I recomputed the number from sqlite instead of trusting the panel: the five imaging_sessions carry avg_guiding_rms 0.65 / 1.10 / 0.70 / 0.55 / 0.60, mean 3.60/5 = 0.7200. equipment_health_service.dart:200 takes `baseline = recentSessions.skip(5).take(10)`, which with exactly five sessions is empty; _mean (line 324) returns 0.0 for an empty iterable and line 207 clamps it to 0.1. 0.7200 / 0.1 = 7.20 exactly, matching the string on screen to both decimals. The HFR trigger is the same shape: recent mean HFR = (2.9+4.2+3.0+2.5+2.2)/5 = 2.96 against a clamped 0.1 baseline at line 213, so 2.96 > 0.115 always fires. Both branches fire for ANY user with 1-5 sessions and non-null guiding/HFR, and they deduct 18 + 14 = 32 points from the health score. Every file:line in the where: checked out (200 baseline, 207/213 the two clamps, the two `if` triggers immediately above the titles at 226/238, _mean at 324); the render site is science_analytics_tab.dart:387. One immaterial slip in the finding's narrative: the newest session is Night E at 0.60, not 0.55 (0.55 is Night D, the second newest) - the arithmetic is unaffected. Severity P1 stands: this is a cry-wolf claim of a 7x mount regression shown to every new user, and the fix is a guard, not a threshold move.

verdicts.title: Stored photometry for a past session is invisible: the light curve is filtered by the CURRENT global target selection, so reviewing any other night shows "has no data yet"
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced by the same A/B, driven myself. With 'Night D - V-Test' selected the Science tab renders 'Differential Photometry has no data yet' and 'Need at least 10 photometry points (0 available)', with no Export to AAVSO button and the guide ladder stuck on rung 2 'Track a star' - while sqlite shows session 4 holds 480 photometry_measurements rows, 120 of them role='target' object_id='V-TEST' with a non-null differential_magnitude on every one. Switching only the session picker to 'Night E - M13' (session 5, 2 light frames) immediately draws a 'Differential Photometry' chart with a dMag axis, surfaces 'Export to AAVSO', and Period Analysis reports 'analyze 80 data points' - because session 5's rows carry object_id='target_primary'. That is the only difference between the two sessions. I closed the loop on the cause from state rather than inference: app_settings holds `science.photometry.target_anchor` = '' (empty), so photometry_selection.dart:205 `selection?.target?.objectId ?? 'target_primary'` yields the literal 'target_primary', and session_products.dart:313 filters `row.objectId == args.$2`. Both cited locations are exact (sessionLightCurveProvider begins at :299, the filter is at :313; activePhotometryTargetObjectIdProvider at :203-205). A stored night's science data is unreachable and un-exportable unless the current live selection happens to name the same object.

verdicts.title: Optical Train Diagnostics grades a session with ZERO data as "A - Excellent" and states "tilt looks controlled" and "center and edge behavior look balanced"
verdicts.location_wrong: The render citation is wrong: the Analytics Diagnostics tab renders DiagnosticsTabContent from packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/diagnostics/diagnostics_screen.dart (analytics_screen.dart:241), and the offending strings live in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/diagnostics/diagnostics_screen/health_summary_cards.dart:26 ('Optical Health'), :178 ('Within range') and :250 ('Score X: tilt looks controlled for this session.') plus diagnostics_screen/optical_alignment_cards.dart:195 ('Edge/center residual ratio') and :208 ('Center and edge behavior look balanced for this session.'). The cited packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/diagnostics/diagnostic_dump_screen.dart exists but contains no optical/tilt code at all - a fixer sent there would find nothing.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed, with a caveat about which session I could reach. On Analytics > Diagnostics the panel for 'Night A - M31' renders, in one view: 'Optical Health / A / Excellent', bars Tilt 0 and Collimation 0, a Tilt card badged 'Within range' reading 'Score 0.0: tilt looks controlled for this session.', a Collimation card badged 'Centered' reading 'Lower is better. Edge/center residual ratio: 0.0' and 'Center and edge behavior look balanced for this session.', a Findings card reading 'No diagnostics data - Capture more solved frames to estimate field tilt and collimation.', and beside them 'PSF Field Map / 0 tiles / No PSF field tile data for this session.' and 'Astrometric Residuals / 0 vectors / No astrometric residual data for this session.' sqlite confirms zero psf_field_tiles rows for that session and an entirely empty astrometry_residual_vectors table. The cause is exactly as stated and I traced it in source: optical_train_diagnostics_service.dart returns `tiltScore: 0, collimationScore: 0` from its `if (psfTiles.isEmpty)` early return, and OpticalHealthScore.fromScores computes overall = 100 - (0*0.5 + 0*0.5) = 100, which clears the aThreshold of 90 - so 'no measurement' is scored identically to 'perfect optics'. Caveat on the repro: I could not render the finding's own session, Night D - V-Test (120 frames); its diagnostics panel sat on loading skeletons for over 2.5 minutes with nothing in the log, so I substituted Night A, which satisfies the finding's own stated repro ('pick any session with no psf_field_tiles rows'). The session-4 DB facts the finding cites are nonetheless correct (0 tiles, 0 vectors). Severity P1 stands - the panel is the surface a user checks when they suspect tilt, and it currently returns a green A on zero evidence. The one mitigation I saw is a small 'Need more solved frames to determine tilt direction' line inside the Tilt card, which the grade and the two verdict sentences contradict.

verdicts.title: Campaign Rollup contradicts itself three ways on one card: "Total integration 0.0h" beside "0.17h integration", and "No frames captured for this target yet" beside a session with 2 frames
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced verbatim. Analytics > Science > M13 campaign card opens 'Campaign Rollup / M13' showing Sessions 1, Total integration 0.0h, First/Last session Jul 31 2026, Mean HFR 2.20, Mean seeing -, Effective imaging 0.0%, then 'Per-filter progress: No frames captured for this target yet.', then a Sessions list with 'Night E - M13 / Jul 31, 2026 23:00 | - | 0.17h integration / HFR 2.20 / RMS 0.60'. I recomputed rather than compared readouts: session 5 (target_id=4 = M13) has exactly 2 captured_images rows, both frame_type='light', exposure_duration 300.0, is_accepted=0, and imaging_sessions.total_integration_secs = 600.0. 600/3600 = 0.1667 -> the 0.17h on the session row; the accepted-light sum is 0.0 -> the 0.0h header. campaign_rollup_service.dart's `_build` computes lightFrames as `frameType == 'light' && i.isAccepted`, feeding both totalCapturedIntegrationSecs (campaign_rollup_dialog.dart:172) and _buildFilters (empty -> the :226 'No frames captured' string), while the per-session row at campaign_rollup_dialog.dart:600 prints session.sessionIntegrationSecs. Both cited files are right. One correction for the fixer: the finding says 'the header tiles ... count only accepted frames', but only Total integration does - Mean HFR 2.20 and Effective imaging 0.0% come from the imaging_sessions rows with no acceptance filter at all, so the card actually mixes three populations, not two. Severity corrected to P2: each number is individually defensible (0.0h really is the accepted integration; 0.17h really is the session's captured integration) and nothing downstream acts on it - the defect is that one card labels two different populations with the same words, most sharply in the flatly false 'No frames captured for this target yet.' It misleads, but unlike the guiding-baseline and optical-health items it does not assert a fault or a clean bill of health.

verdicts.title: Sequencer crash-recovery checkpoint is stored outside the profile data dir, so one instance offers to resume another instance's sequence
verdicts.location_wrong: The `where` (app_shell.dart:347-348 getApplicationSupportDirectory -> sequencerSetCheckpointDir; checkpoint.rs:516) is exact. The `unit` is not: this is filed under screen:analytics/session_tab.dart and has nothing to do with the Session tab or Analytics - it is app startup.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by direct experiment, not inference. First, my own instance's log line 15 reads 'Setting checkpoint directory to: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop' even though SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR / SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR both point at /tmp/ns-audit/v-analytics/data - app_shell.dart:347's getApplicationSupportDirectory() ignores both. Then I proved the read side: I planted a resumable checkpoint (sequence id 'claude-noop-probe', name 'NOOP CONTRACT PROBE') at ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint - i.e. the file another instance would have written - and restarted my app against a database with `select count(*) from sequences` = 0 and `sequence_checkpoints` = 0. It came up on 'Recover Sequence? / A previous sequence was interrupted and can be resumed. / Sequence NOOP CONTRACT PROBE / Saved 0m ago / Completed 4 frames (0m integration)' with a live Resume button, for a sequence that does not exist anywhere in its own database. I removed the planted file afterwards. Two corrections. (1) The finding's justification - 'on a machine that runs both the desktop app and the headless host (a shipped configuration) the two silently clobber each other' - does not hold as written: app_shell.dart is the ONLY caller of sequencerSetCheckpointDir in the whole app (the headless entry point never sets it, and app_shell's `backend is! NetworkBackend` guard already avoids pushing this path at a remote host), so I could not establish the desktop/headless collision. The collision I actually reproduced needs two local instances with different SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR values, which is the audit harness's configuration rather than a shipped one. (2) I cannot corroborate the secondary 'Completed 4 frames (0m integration)' observation - in my run those figures came from the values I planted, so that line proves nothing about the writer. Severity corrected to P2: the durable defect is that crash-recovery state is not scoped to the database it references, so the app will offer to resume a sequence absent from the active DB, but the single-instance shipped path recovers correctly and no data is destroyed.
